title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The setting is cosimplicial k-modules indexed by the standard simplices Δ^N.

**Objects.**
- L_* is the cosimplicial module N ↦ k^{Δ^N} ≅ k^{N+1}. Think of it as the linear forms in the barycentric coordinates t_0,…,t_N. Equivalently it is the 0-cochains on Δ^N.
- Ψ_* ⊂ L_* is the rank-N submodule of constant-coefficient 1-forms dt_i, subject to Σ dt_i = 0. Equivalently it is the augmentation kernel.
- Γ^p L_* is the homogeneous degree-p divided-power polynomials.
- Λ^q Ψ_* is the constant q-forms.
- So Γ^p L ⊗ Λ^q Ψ is the degree-p, form-degree-q piece of the PD polynomial de Rham complex of the cosimplicial affine simplex. This is the PD analogue of Sullivan/Cartan polynomial forms ∇(p,•).
- On the other side, C^m_* = Λ^{m+1} L_*: at level N this is Λ^{m+1} k^{N+1}. The next page identifies it as k^{Inj(Δ^m,Δ^N)}, i.e. the simplicial m-cochains of Δ^N.

**The diagram.** The top diagram arranges the rows
- Λ^{n-1}Ψ → L⊗Λ^{n-1}Ψ → Λ^n L, where the first map T_1 is a mono and the second is the wedge;
- similarly Γ^2 L ⊗ Λ^{n-2}Ψ → Λ^{n-1} L.

These relate the PD-form pieces to the cochain modules C^{n-1}_*, C^{n-2}_*, etc.

**Rank count.** The rest of the page is a rank count, to test whether Γ^p L ⊗ Λ^q Ψ admits a filtration whose graded pieces are copies of the C^m_*.
- First, rk(Γ^p L_(N) ⊗ Λ^q Ψ_(N)) = C(N+p,p)·C(N,q) = c_{p,q}·C(N+p,p+q), with c_{p,q} = C(p+q,p).
- Special cases checked on the page:
  - (N+1)C(N,n-1) = n·C(N+1,n);
  - C(N+2,2)·C(N,n-2) = C(n,2)·C(N+2,n).
- Put φ_r(N) = rk Λ^r L_(N) = C(N+1,r), and let τ be the shift (τP)(n) = P(n+1).
- Pascal's rule gives τφ_r = φ_r + φ_{r-1}, hence τ^p φ_r = Σ_i C(p,i) φ_{r-i}. The page computes τ^2 and τ^3 explicitly.
- Since C(N+p,p+q) = φ_{p+q}(N+p-1) = τ^{p-1}φ_{p+q}(N), we get
  rk(Γ^p L ⊗ Λ^q Ψ) = c_{p,q}·Σ_{i=0}^{p-1} C(p-1,i)·rk Λ^{p+q-i} L.

**Conclusion (heuristic).** In the Grothendieck group of cosimplicial modules (dimension-wise), Γ^p L ⊗ Λ^q Ψ ~ c_{p,q}·(Λ^{p+q}L + (p-1)Λ^{p+q-1}L + C(p-1,2)Λ^{p+q-2}L + … + Λ^{q+1}L). That is, a sum of shifted cochain modules C^{p+q-1-i}_*.

The aim is presumably a PD Poincaré lemma / de Rham theorem on the cosimplicial simplex. The idea is to compute the cohomotopy of each PD-form piece by filtering it by modules of the type Λ^{m+1}L, whose cohomotopy is known from the next page (k in one or two adjacent degrees).
errors: The line 'φ_{p+q}(N+p) = φ_{p+q}(N+p-1) + 2φ…' is an abandoned false start: the second term should be φ_{p+q-1}(N+p-1), with no factor 2.

There is a minor index slip in the shift. The page writes c_{p,q} τ^p φ_{p+q}(N+1) (reading uncertain), whereas with φ_r(N) = C(N+1,r) one needs τ^{p-1}φ_{p+q}(N). The final line correctly uses τ^{p-1}.
Only ranks are matched. The existence of an actual cosimplicial filtration with these graded pieces is not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial PD polynomial de Rham forms on the standard simplices, Γ^p L_* ⊗ Λ^q Ψ_*, compared with the simplicial cochain cosimplicial modules Λ^{m+1} L_*
ideas.modern_name: PD (divided power) analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial de Rham forms; simplicial de Rham theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), Cartan (1976) in characteristic 0; divided-power variants in later work on integral/p-adic rational homotopy (e.g. Cenkl–Porter-type or Mandell-type approaches), but unsure of exact credits
ideas.where_published: unsure; the 1976 IHES lecture itself apparently was not published

ideas.what: Rank identity C(N+p,p)C(N,q) = C(p+q,p)C(N+p,p+q), and its expansion via the shift operator into ranks of Λ^r L
Mono T_1: Λ^{n-1}Ψ → L⊗Λ^{n-1}Ψ, followed by the wedge to Λ^n L, linking the forms pieces to the cochain modules

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks a filtration of the PD form pieces Γ^pL⊗Λ^qΨ on cosimplicial simplices with graded pieces c_{p,q}C(p-1,i) copies of the cochain modules Λ^{p+q-i}L. This would be a route to a PD simplicial de Rham theorem valid over any ring. Only the rank count is done here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor detail of an approach to integral or characteristic-p simplicial de Rham comparison with divided powers. The explicit multiplicities could be of mild interest, but the statement is essentially combinatorial.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine binomial bookkeeping supporting a PD simplicial de Rham comparison. The overall programme (the unpublished 1976 lecture) is of historical interest, but this page contains no new result beyond a rank heuristic.
transcription_corrections: 'L^1_* ⊗ Λ^{n-2}Ψ_*' at the start of the third row is probably Ψ_* ⊗ Λ^{n-2}Ψ_* or Λ^{n-1}Ψ-related; it is unclear in the image.
The bottom expression is better read as '(Λ^n L_* + Λ^{n-1}L_*)^{n(n-1)/2}', i.e. a sum with multiplicity C(n,2), matching the rank identity below it.
'= c_{p,q} τ^p φ_{p+q}(N+1)' is likely τ^{p-1} in the image (superscript 'p-1' is partly visible).
